how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Credit Card Issuance and Operation Rules are the binding instrument; the FAQ is interpretive guidance clarifying application, not creating new obligations.
The FAQ references the Rules to resolve ambiguity; where they conflict, the Rules prevail as the enforceable source.
Decision use: rely on the Rules for the legal requirement and treat FAQ answers as SAMA's interpretive position on scope and application.

144.theme: Governance/conduct rules on how SAMA-supervised entities may host or sponsor external events, addressing conflicts of interest, gifts/hospitality, and reputational conduct.
how_members_connect: Two near-identical instances of the same rule set (original and a duplicate copy) linked only by semantic similarity.
For compliance use, treat as a single controlling standard; verify which version is the operative/current SAMA issuance before relying on either.
No hierarchy or cross-reference between them — the duplication is a data artefact, not a distinct obligation.

145.theme: Physical security standards for the financial sector, specifying CCTV technical requirements tied to defined surveillance purposes.
how_members_connect: The specifications document references the surveillance objectives, so the technical requirements (camera quality, coverage) are scoped by the intended function.
Objectives define graded terms — Identification, Recognition, Detection — that set the compliance benchmark each installed system must meet.
Decision consequence: an entity's CCTV adequacy is assessed against the objective category applicable to a given zone, not a single uniform spec.

146.theme: Credit-risk capital/provisioning inputs, linking eligible collateral recognition to Loss Given Default estimation under the risk framework.
how_members_connect: Eligible Collateral and Valuation references LGD: recognized, properly valued collateral reduces the LGD applied to an exposure.
Defined eligibility and valuation criteria act as a scope limit — only collateral meeting those standards may lower LGD.
Consequence for compliance: mis-valued or ineligible collateral cannot be used to reduce provisioning/capital, affecting credit-risk calculations.

147.theme: Consumer-protection/conduct controls on debt collection practices, with specific application to individual borrowers and real estate financiers.
how_members_connect: The collection-controls circular is conceptually related to the real estate financier obligations circular — collection conduct duties overlap where real estate finance is extended to individuals.
Both operate in the finance-company/consumer regime, constraining how financiers may pursue individual customers.
Decision consequence: a real estate financier must satisfy both its sector-specific obligations and the general individual-customer collection controls when recovering from individual borrowers.

148.theme: AML/CTF operational obligations tying transaction record retention to funds-transfer traceability requirements. Covers the recordkeeping and originator/beneficiary information duties central to the wire-transfer ('travel rule') regime.
how_members_connect: Wire Transfer references Record Keeping because transfer messages and their originator/beneficiary data must be retained for the mandated period to satisfy AML/CTF audit and law-enforcement access.
The linkage makes recordkeeping the evidentiary backbone of wire-transfer compliance: failure to retain transfer data breaches both obligations.
Read together as enforceable duties on ordering, intermediary, and beneficiary institutions handling cross-border and domestic transfers.

149.theme: Real estate financing regulation governing the transfer/assignment of mortgage debts and the contractual terms subjecting such financing to SAMA rules.
how_members_connect: The Time Periods Circular references the Contract Subjection Circular, imposing deadlines/timeframes on the debt-transfer process for contracts already scoped under SAMA supervision.
Hierarchy: the subjection circular fixes which financing contracts fall within scope; the time-periods circular then imposes procedural obligations on transferring those in-scope debts.
Decision-useful for finance companies/banks assessing timing obligations when assigning real estate financing portfolios.

150.theme: CDD/identity-verification guidance permitting reliance on government digital credentials (Absher/Tawakkalna) for customer and family-status verification within KYC obligations.
how_members_connect: Both instruments authorize acceptance of state-issued digital documents as valid identity evidence; the Family Record item references the Digital ID item as a companion verification source.
Together they define acceptable means of satisfying identification/verification requirements without requiring physical documents.
Scope note: reliance is on official government-issued digital IDs, distinct from third-party CDD reliance regimes.

151.theme: Prudential disclosure regime for Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB), pairing qualitative governance disclosure with mandated quantitative reporting.
how_members_connect: Template IRRBB1 (quantitative figures) references Table IRRBBA (risk-management objectives/policies) so numbers are read against the bank's stated IRRBB governance.
Hierarchy of disclosure: the qualitative table frames methodology and assumptions that the quantitative template must reflect.
Both are Pillar 3-style disclosure obligations; incomplete or inconsistent pairing undermines regulatory transparency requirements.

152.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure templates reconciling financial-statement (accounting) scope of consolidation with the prudential/regulatory scope used for capital purposes. This covers the bank's obligation to explain why balance-sheet carrying values differ from regulatory exposure amounts.
how_members_connect: LI1 maps accounting vs regulatory consolidation scopes; LI2 explains the drivers of exposure-amount differences that LI1 surfaces.
The 'references' link is an explanatory chain: LI2 elaborates the sources behind the reconciliation LI1 presents, so both must be read together for a coherent disclosure.
Both are subordinate reporting instruments implementing SAMA's adoption of the Basel Pillar 3 framework.

153.theme: Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) disclosure under SAMA's Pillar 3 regime — the obligation to describe governance/measurement of IRRBB and to report quantitative sensitivity figures.
how_members_connect: Table IRRBBA sets qualitative disclosure of IRRBB management (governance, assumptions, hedging); Template IRRBB1 reports the quantitative outcomes.
The 'references' link means the numbers in IRRBB1 are only interpretable against the modelling assumptions and controls disclosed in IRRBBA — read as one disclosure package.
Both implement SAMA's adoption of the Basel IRRBB standard; qualitative context is a precondition for meaningful quantitative reporting.

154.theme: Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) creditor-hierarchy disclosures for resolution planning — showing where TLAC-eligible instruments rank in insolvency at the resolution-entity and material-subgroup levels.
how_members_connect: TLAC3 discloses creditor ranking at the resolution entity; TLAC2 does so at material subgroup entities — parallel templates covering different points in the group structure.
The 'references' link ties subgroup rankings to the resolution-entity ranking so the loss-absorption waterfall can be read across the group.
Both are subordinate resolution/prudential reporting instruments under SAMA's TLAC framework.

155.theme: Bank obligations to respond to requests from judicial and dispute-resolution bodies — the duty and procedure for supplying information to courts and the Banking Dispute Committee.
how_members_connect: The SAMA Circular sets the overarching obligation for responding to judicial authorities; the Banking Dispute Committee response requirement is a specific application of it.
The 'cites' link makes the Committee-response provision subordinate to and dependent on the general circular for its authority and procedure.
Together they scope who may compel bank disclosures and the compliance duty to respond — relevant to bank-secrecy exceptions and lawful-request handling.

156.theme: Physical currency-handling controls: authentication of banknotes and use of official denomination reference materials by cash-handling institutions.
how_members_connect: Both address genuine-currency verification; the denomination card templates supply the reference features against which the banknote inspection obligation is discharged.
Link is conceptual, not hierarchical — neither instrument scopes or amends the other; the templates operationalize the inspection duty.

157.theme: Payment-transaction fraud prevention tied to customer authentication — relevant to payments/PSP and card-acquiring risk controls.
how_members_connect: Identity verification via a trusted source functions as the front-end control that mitigates the fraud vectors arising in preauthorization/advice transactions.
Relationship is conceptual: reliable customer verification reduces exposure to the described fraud, but neither provision defines the other.

158.theme: Licensing and operational conditions for exchange centers, including premises standards and a scope-limited customer-ID exemption in the airport context.
how_members_connect: Minimum premises requirements set the baseline for exchange center operation; the airport ID exemption is a scope limitation to CDD/identification duties for that specific setting.
Note the exemption is narrow and does not displace general AML/KYC obligations outside its defined airport scope.

159.theme: Saudization (labor-nationalization) obligations imposed on exchange companies, including counting rules for eligible nationals.
how_members_connect: The Saudization obligation sets the workforce-nationalization requirement for exchange companies; the child-counting rule cross-references it to clarify how a citizen's child is credited toward that quota.
Link is a 'references' relationship — the counting rule interprets/supplements the primary Saudization requirement rather than creating a separate duty.

160.theme: Prudential and accounting conduct standards for licensed money changers, binding the sectoral rulebook to specific external-audit/accounting expectations.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Rules Governing Money Changing Business set the primary licensing/conduct regime; the Circular on External Auditor Accounting Standards is a subordinate instruction operating within that regime.
The circular references the Rules to specify accounting/audit standards money changers' external auditors must apply — read as an enforceable reporting obligation, not guidance.
Compliance consequence: money changers must satisfy both the general conduct rules and the audit-standard circular; the circular narrows how financial statements are prepared and verified.

161.theme: Recovery/repossession rights over leased movable assets under the finance-lease regime, linking the enabling law to SAMA's operational instruction.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Finance Lease Law is the primary statute; the Circular on Recovery of Leased Movable Assets is subordinate implementing detail.
The circular references the Law to authorize and condition how lessors recover leased movables — treat the circular as setting the permissible recovery procedure.
Compliance consequence: repossession must be exercised within the statutory lease framework as operationalized by the circular; deviation risks unlawful recovery.

162.theme: Operational-continuity and holiday scheduling obligations for licensed finance companies under the Finance Companies Control Law.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Finance Companies Control Law is the enabling statute; the Circular on Finance Company Holidays is a subordinate directive issued under SAMA's supervisory authority.
The circular references the Control Law as its legal basis for prescribing holiday/closure arrangements.
Compliance consequence: finance companies must align working-day and closure practices with the circular; relevant for consumer-facing timing, payment due dates, and grace-period calculations.

163.theme: Real estate finance rules as applied to land financing, connecting the primary law to a circular that clarifies scope and conditions for financing land.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Real Estate Finance Law is the primary statute; the Circular on Land Financing is subordinate interpretive/scoping detail under the Real Estate Finance Regulation.
The circular references the Law to define when and how land (as distinct from built property) may be financed — read as a scope condition on permissible products.
Compliance consequence: lenders must confirm land-financing offerings fall within the circular's conditions before treating them as compliant real estate finance.

164.theme: Real estate mortgage registration regime: the statutory framework for registering property mortgages and SAMA's operational instruction that registration reflect the actual contractual terms. Relevant to secured-lending and finance-company collateral perfection decisions.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Registered Real Estate Mortgage Law is the primary statute; the circular is a subordinate SAMA instruction implementing/directing compliance.
The circular references the Law to require that mortgage registration match contract reality — an obligation on lenders to register mortgages consistent with the underlying financing agreement.
Legal consequence: collateral validity/enforceability depends on registration conforming to both the statute and the circular's fidelity-to-contract requirement.

165.theme: White Land (vacant land) fees regime: statutory levy on undeveloped urban land and SAMA guidance on treatment of fee-liable lands. Relevant where such land serves as financing collateral or affects borrower obligations.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the White Land Fees Law is the governing statute; the circular is subordinate SAMA guidance referencing it.
The circular references the Law to direct how supervised entities register/treat lands subject to the white-land fee.
Legal consequence: outstanding statutory fees on such land bear on lien priority, collateral valuation, and registration obligations.

166.theme: Controls governing execution of banking-procedure transactions through SAMA's interbank system. Governance/operational-risk regime for how supervised banks process transactions.
how_members_connect: The circular imposes SAMA-set controls on banking procedure transactions and references the SAMA Net System as the channel/infrastructure to which those controls attach.
Legal consequence: banks must observe the prescribed controls when transacting via SAMA Net; the system reference scopes where the obligation applies.

167.theme: Saudization/labor regime as applied to supervised entities: national-employment and recruitment-contracting obligations flowing from the Labor Law. Relevant to institutional compliance beyond core prudential rules.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Labor Law is the primary statute; the circular is a subordinate SAMA instruction referencing it.
The circular references the Law to impose obligations on supervised entities regarding employing nationals and recruitment contracting.
Legal consequence: labor-law compliance (nationalization, recruitment terms) is a supervisory expectation, not solely a Ministry of Labor matter.

168.theme: SAMA's regime for publicly disclosing enforcement actions against banks, linking the disclosure mechanism to a standardized taxonomy of violation types.
how_members_connect: The publication Instructions govern when and how SAMA discloses banking penalties, and reference the Classification Guide to categorize each published violation.
Hierarchy: the Guide functions as a subordinate classification aid to the operative disclosure Instructions.
Decision-usefulness: a bank assessing reputational/enforcement exposure reads the Instructions for disclosure triggers and the Guide to understand how a given breach will be labelled publicly.

169.theme: Consumer-facing disclosure obligations for finance companies, tying a mandated contract summary document to the governing implementing regulation under the Finance Companies Control Law.
how_members_connect: The Finance Contract Summary Form is the prescribed disclosure instrument required under the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law.
Hierarchy: Law -> Implementing Regulation -> mandated Form; the Regulation is the enforceable source, the Form the compliance artifact.
Decision-usefulness: finance companies must issue the summary to borrowers per the Regulation's terms; the Form defines the minimum disclosure content.

170.theme: Framework governing primary dealers in the Saudi government securities market and their interaction with the sovereign debt issuer.
how_members_connect: The Primary Dealer Guidelines set the eligibility and conduct obligations for dealers and reference the DMO as the issuing/managing authority.
Institutional linkage: the DMO is the counterparty/authority the Guidelines operationalize around.
Decision-usefulness: a market participant reads the Guidelines to understand primary dealer duties and the DMO's role in the issuance framework.

171.theme: Data protection/information security controls for permanent destruction of data, distinguishing related but distinct disposal concepts.
how_members_connect: Secure Disposal references Secure Erase as a defined method/subset within the broader disposal control.
Definitional relationship: one term scopes or is a component of the other, so the correct standard depends on which is required.
Decision-usefulness: apply the specific defined term SAMA guidance invokes to determine the required destruction standard for regulated data.

172.theme: Accounting treatment of zakat and income tax in the financial statements of SAMA-supervised entities, anchored to the accounting framework SAMA mandates.
how_members_connect: The Circular is the operative SAMA instruction on how to account for zakat and income tax; it references IFRS as adopted by SAMA as the governing accounting basis.
Compliance consequence: entities must reconcile zakat/tax accounting to the SAMA-adopted IFRS baseline rather than IFRS as issued by the IASB, so any local carve-outs or SAMA overlays control.

173.theme: Prudential liquidity risk management expectations for banks, transposing international standards into a SAMA supervisory instrument.
how_members_connect: The SAMA Circular cites the BCBS Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk (2008) as its source framework.

Legal linkage is transposition: the BCBS Principles are non-binding international guidance, but they become enforceable in KSA through the SAMA Circular — read obligations from the Circular, with the BCBS text as interpretive context.

174.theme: Capital adequacy regime — the countercyclical capital buffer as a component of the Basel III capital stack applied to KSA banks.
how_members_connect: The CCyB provision cites Basel III Capital Standards as its parent framework, situating it as a subordinate, regime-specific buffer within the broader capital standards.

Compliance consequence: the CCyB requirement must be read together with the base Basel III minimum ratios and other buffers as SAMA calibrates them; the buffer is variable and set by supervisory judgment.

175.theme: Interest rate risk in the banking book — a Pillar 2 / supervisory risk regime for measuring and managing IRRBB in KSA banks.
how_members_connect: The SAMA IRRBB rules cite the Basel IRRBB Standard (2016) as their source, transposing its measurement and disclosure expectations.
Legal linkage: the Basel standard supplies the substantive methodology, but enforceable obligations derive from SAMA's adoption; apply the standard as implemented locally, not in the abstract.

176.theme: BNPL licensing authority derives from the Finance Companies Control Law; this cluster covers who may lawfully offer BNPL and the entry requirements for authorization.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Finance Companies Control Law is the primary statute; the BNPL License Application Guidelines are subordinate SAMA guidance operationalizing entry into the regulated finance-company perimeter.
The Guidelines cite the Law as the source of SAMA's licensing power — a BNPL provider must satisfy statutory finance-company conditions plus the application criteria.
Decision consequence: unlicensed BNPL activity is a licensing breach under the Law, not merely non-conformance with a guide.

177.theme: Governance allocation within the operational-risk regime — the internal roles and committee accountable for identifying and managing operational risk.
how_members_connect: The Operational Risk Management Committee is the oversight body; the Operational Risk Manager is the executing function reporting into it.
The reference edge reflects an obligation chain: the Manager discharges day-to-day duties while the Committee holds governance accountability.
Decision consequence: firms must be able to show both roles exist and are distinct for governance adequacy.

178.theme: Consumer-facing disclosure standards for bank savings products, centered on standardized rate presentation.
how_members_connect: The General Rules for Savings Products in Banks are the binding requirement; the Annual Equivalent Rate (AER) is a defined disclosure metric mandated within them.
The reference edge fixes AER as the required, comparable rate-expression banks must disclose to depositors.
Decision consequence: savings-product terms must present returns via the defined AER to meet the Rules' transparency obligation.

179.theme: Payment-acceptance pricing and QR-based instruments within the merchant payments/POS-e-commerce space.
how_members_connect: The QR Code Payments Development Project and the Unified Pricing Model for POS and E-commerce are conceptually linked as parts of SAMA's merchant-acceptance framework.
The link is thematic rather than a strict hierarchy — pricing rules for POS/e-commerce inform the economics of QR acceptance channels.
Decision consequence: QR payment offerings fall within the same merchant-acquiring pricing discipline as POS and e-commerce.

180.theme: Governance of bank/PSP-originated SMS notifications to customers, covering both permitted sender-name identification and the mandatory content elements of customer messages. Sits within consumer-protection and operational-conduct rules.
how_members_connect: Two SAMA circulars addressing the same conduct area: one governs approved SMS sender names/identifiers, the other mandates the unified data elements a customer notification must contain.
Linked as conceptually related — together they set enforceable minimum requirements for how supervised entities notify customers by SMS.
Neither is a subordinate of the other; read them as parallel obligations that a compliant messaging practice must satisfy simultaneously.

181.theme: Information/cyber security control obligations for supervised entities, spanning general cyber-security controls and the more specific data-focused cybersecurity controls framework (DCC-1:2022). Part of the governance/risk and operational-resilience regime.
how_members_connect: The Cyber Security Controls Circular sets the baseline institution-wide security obligations; DCC-1:2022 layers additional data-classification and data-protection controls on top.
Linked as conceptually related — DCC-1 should be read as complementary/more granular to the general controls, not as a replacement.
Compliance decisions must treat both as concurrently applicable minimum standards where each is in scope for the entity.

182.theme: Statutory basis for SAMA's prudential supervision of banks and the procedural rules for enforcing judicial decisions against/through banks. Bridges the primary banking law and its operational enforcement guidance.
how_members_connect: The Banking Control Law is the primary statute; the Judicial Decisions Enforcement Procedures Circular is subordinate guidance that references and operates within that legal authority.
Hierarchy runs law -> circular: the circular derives its enforceability from the Banking Control Law and does not expand SAMA's statutory powers.
Use the Law to establish supervisory jurisdiction/obligation and the circular for the specific procedure banks must follow when handling enforcement of judicial decisions.

183.theme: Top-of-hierarchy instruments of Saudi law — a Royal Decree and a Council of Ministers Resolution — that provide the legislative foundation from which SAMA regulations and circulars derive authority.
how_members_connect: The Royal Decree and the Council of Ministers Resolution are linked by cross-reference, reflecting the standard KSA enactment chain (Resolution approves/enacts, Decree promulgates).
These are primary legal sources: subordinate SAMA regulations, rules, and circulars must be traced back to instruments at this level for their legal validity.
For legal decisions, treat these as the controlling authority — any lower-tier guidance cannot override or exceed what these instruments authorize.

184.theme: Governance/remuneration disclosure regime: periodic reporting to SAMA of total remuneration paid to board members and board committees, supporting supervisory oversight of pay practices.
how_members_connect: Single-member community; obligation is a standalone reporting duty owed by the supervised entity to SAMA.
Legal consequence: sits within governance/remuneration controls — non-submission or inaccurate reporting is a supervisory compliance breach.

185.theme: SAMA circular directing/permitting supervised entities' handling of donations to the King Salman Relief Center; a specific instruction rather than a broad regime.
how_members_connect: Single-member community; the circular is the operative instruction with no internal cross-links.
Compliance relevance: treat as a discrete directive; any donation-processing obligation flows from this circular alone, not a wider framework.

186.theme: Operational/e-government integration directive establishing an electronic link with Elm for digital document services, relevant to identity/document verification inputs.
how_members_connect: Single-member community; standalone instruction authorizing or requiring use of the Elm digital document channel.
Legal relevance: may support CDD/identity-verification reliance, but its scope is limited to what this circular specifies — do not extend beyond stated document services.

187.theme: Data-protection/confidentiality control prohibiting the use of social media channels for exchanging (customer or business) data, part of information-security and confidentiality obligations.
how_members_connect: Single-member community; a prohibition imposing a direct restriction on the supervised entity's data-handling conduct.
Compliance consequence: use of social media for covered data exchange is a defined breach; interacts with broader confidentiality/data-protection duties even though no internal edges are shown.

188.theme: Governance/fit-and-proper regime: SAMA's requirements for appointing persons to senior/controlled positions in supervised entities. Covers who must obtain non-objection/approval before appointment and the standing eligibility criteria.
how_members_connect: Single-member node: 'Update of Senior Position Appointment Requirements' — a SAMA instrument revising prior fit-and-proper appointment conditions.
As a governance obligation, it binds supervised institutions to seek SAMA clearance before filling designated senior roles.
No internal edges present; treat as standalone until linked to the underlying appointment/licensing rules it amends.

189.theme: Unclassified SAMA circular identified only by reference number; regime cannot be determined from the node alone.
how_members_connect: Single-member node 'SAMA Circular 10241' with no internal edges.
A circular sits low in the hierarchy (law -> regulation -> circular -> guide) and typically operationalizes or clarifies a parent instrument.
Subject matter and obligation content are not derivable from provided context; do not infer scope without the linked source.

190.theme: Physical security/operational-risk regime: SAMA requirements for deploying security surveillance camera systems at supervised premises (e.g., branches, ATMs).
how_members_connect: Single-member node 'Security Surveillance Cameras System Application' — a technical/operational security obligation on institutions.
Functions as a control requirement; likely intersects with fraud-prevention and premises-security expectations rather than AML/CTF proper.
No internal edges; standalone security-standards instrument in the provided graph.

191.theme: Payments regime: rules governing the GCC-NET point-of-sale payment service, i.e., cross-GCC card acceptance/interoperability at merchant POS terminals under SAMA's payment-system oversight.
how_members_connect: Single-member node 'GCC-NET POS Payment Service' defining a specific payment scheme/service.
Sits within the PSP/payments regulatory space, engaging merchant acceptance and settlement obligations.
No internal edges present; link to broader payment-services and card-scheme rules to establish obligation chains.

192.theme: Administrative circular establishing SAMA's electronic services portal (eSAMA) as the channel through which supervised entities interact with the regulator.
how_members_connect: Single-member community; no internal linkage to other nodes in the provided context.
Operates as a procedural/administrative instrument rather than a substantive prudential or conduct obligation.

193.theme: Administrative circular designating the Founding Day as an official holiday, affecting settlement, deadlines, and working-day calculations across supervised entities.
how_members_connect: Single-member community with no internal edges provided.
Relevant only as a calendar/timing rule that may shift regulatory or contractual deadlines; not a substantive regime obligation.

194.theme: Regulation governing enforceability of netting and collateral arrangements, central to counterparty credit-risk mitigation and close-out treatment in the KSA financial sector.
how_members_connect: Single-member community; no internal cross-references supplied in context.
Sits in the governance/risk and prudential space, defining legal certainty for set-off and collateral rather than imposing conduct duties on consumers or customers.

195.theme: Standalone SAMA circular (10395) whose regime cannot be characterized further from the provided context.
how_members_connect: Single-member community with no internal edges.
No linked definitions, obligations, or hierarchy available to place it within a specific regime; treat scope as undetermined pending the circular's own text.

196.theme: Operational directive from SAMA setting reduced working hours for supervised entities during Ramadan and Eid. Governance/administrative regime rather than prudential or conduct rules.
how_members_connect: Single-member community; a standalone SAMA circular imposing a time-limited administrative obligation on regulated entities' working hours.

272.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of counterparty credit risk (CCR) arising specifically from credit derivative positions. This sits within the Basel-aligned SAMA capital/disclosure regime for banks.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Template CCR6 is a prescribed disclosure format, not a standalone obligation source; it is subordinate to SAMA's adopted Basel Pillar 3 disclosure framework.
Links conceptually to other CCR templates (CCR7, CCRA) as the credit-derivative slice of the same CCR exposure regime.

273.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of period-on-period movement in risk-weighted assets for CCR exposures calculated under the Internal Model Method (IMM). Part of SAMA's capital adequacy disclosure regime for internally-modelled banks.
how_members_connect: Single-member: Template CCR7 applies only to banks with SAMA-approved IMM permission, scoping its use narrowly.
Feeds from and cross-references the qualitative CCR context in Table CCRA and the exposure templates in the same CCR disclosure suite.

274.theme: Qualitative narrative disclosure explaining a bank's CCR risk management objectives, policies and methodologies. Provides the interpretive context for the quantitative CCR templates under SAMA's Pillar 3 regime.
how_members_connect: Single-member: Table CCRA is the qualitative anchor that frames the quantitative CCR6 and CCR7 templates.
Subordinate to SAMA's adopted Basel disclosure standard; imposes a narrative-disclosure requirement rather than a capital-calculation rule.

275.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of specialised lending exposures risk-weighted under the IRB supervisory slotting approach. Sits in SAMA's credit risk capital disclosure regime for banks using internal ratings.
how_members_connect: Single-member: Template CR10 applies only where a bank uses the IRB slotting approach for specialised lending, limiting its scope.
Belongs to the credit-risk (CR) disclosure family, distinct from but parallel to the CCR templates; both are subordinate to SAMA's adopted Basel Pillar 3 framework.

276.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of how credit derivatives used as credit risk mitigation (CRM) affect risk-weighted assets under the Internal Ratings-Based (IRB) approach. Covers the quantitative disclosure obligation for banks recognising credit-protection instruments.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Template CR7 imposes a standardized disclosure requirement for the RWA impact of credit derivatives recognised as CRM under IRB.
Sits within SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework; conceptually linked to broader IRB credit-risk and CRM disclosure templates/tables (e.g., CR8, CRC).
Scope limited to credit derivatives used as protection — not general counterparty exposures.

277.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of period-over-period movements (flow) in credit-risk RWA computed under the IRB approach, showing drivers of RWA change.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Template CR8 imposes an obligation to disclose an RWA flow statement for IRB credit-risk exposures.
Complements CR7 (community 276) within the IRB quantitative-disclosure set; both operate under the same Pillar 3 governance/risk regime.
Purely a reporting/transparency obligation, not a capital-calculation rule itself.

278.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure establishing a bank's overall credit-risk management approach — the narrative foundation for the quantitative credit-risk templates.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Table CRA imposes a qualitative disclosure obligation describing credit-risk strategy, governance and management.
Acts as the contextual/definitional anchor for the quantitative IRB templates (CR7, CR8) and the CRM disclosure (CRC).
Governance/risk-disclosure obligation; frames how later numerical disclosures should be interpreted.

279.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure of the credit risk mitigation (CRM) techniques a bank relies on, describing eligibility, collateral and guarantee/derivative use.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Table CRC imposes a qualitative disclosure obligation on CRM policies and techniques.
Provides the narrative counterpart to quantitative CRM templates such as CR7 (community 276); the two should be read together.
Shares the credit-risk disclosure regime with CRA (general qualitative) and the IRB flow/effect templates.

280.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure regime for banks' reliance on External Credit Assessment Institutions (ECAIs) under the standardised approach to credit risk. Governs transparency obligations about how external ratings map to risk weights.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: Table CRD sets the disclosure template banks must complete when using external credit ratings for regulatory capital.
Subordinate to SAMA's capital adequacy/Pillar 3 disclosure framework; obligation is to explain the use and mapping of nominated ECAIs, not to set risk weights themselves.

281.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure regime for banks permitted to use Internal Ratings-Based (IRB) approaches for credit risk capital. Covers transparency around internally modelled risk parameters.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: Template CRE prescribes qualitative disclosures on IRB model scope, governance, and parameter estimation.
Applies only to banks with SAMA approval to use IRB; distinct from the standardised/external-rating regime (Table CRD) as an alternative capital measurement basis.

282.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure regime for Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) risk capital — counterparty credit risk arising from potential deterioration of derivative counterparties.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: Table CVAA sets general qualitative disclosure requirements for a bank's CVA risk management and capital treatment.
Serves as the umbrella CVA disclosure, with Table CVAB (community 283) as the approach-specific counterpart for the standardised (SA-CVA) method.

283.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure regime specific to the Standardised Approach for CVA risk (SA-CVA), a more risk-sensitive method requiring SAMA approval.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: Table CVAB prescribes qualitative disclosures for banks using SA-CVA.
Subordinate/complementary to the general CVA disclosure (Table CVAA, community 282); SA-CVA use is conditional on supervisory approval, so CVAB applies only to that subset of banks.

284.theme: Prudential disclosure of asset encumbrance, covering the extent to which a bank's assets are pledged or otherwise unavailable to unsecured creditors. Relevant to liquidity risk and resolution planning under SAMA's Pillar 3 / disclosure regime.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: the ENC template is a standalone reporting instrument requiring structured disclosure of encumbered vs. unencumbered assets.
No internal linkages present; compliance obligation is to complete and submit the template as prescribed.

285.theme: Identification of Global Systemically Important Banks through mandated indicator reporting (size, interconnectedness, complexity, cross-jurisdictional activity). Feeds systemic-risk classification and any resulting capital surcharge obligations.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: the GSIB1 template captures the indicator set used for G-SIB assessment.
No internal edges; obligation is submission of the specified systemic indicators.

286.theme: Qualitative liquidity risk management disclosure — governance, funding strategy, and stress-testing of a bank's liquidity position under SAMA's liquidity framework.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Table LIQA is the narrative/qualitative disclosure companion to quantitative liquidity metrics.
No internal linkages; obligation is descriptive disclosure of liquidity risk governance.

287.theme: Market risk capital computation under the simplified standardised approach, available to institutions meeting eligibility thresholds as an alternative to the full standardised approach.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Template MR3 reports market risk capital under the simplified method.
No internal edges; use is scoped to firms qualifying for the simplified approach.

288.theme: Pillar 3 market-risk qualitative disclosure obligation (Table MRA) under SAMA's disclosure framework, requiring banks to narrate their market-risk management strategy, governance, and scope.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Table MRA imposes a standalone qualitative disclosure duty for market risk.
Sits within the market-risk disclosure regime; substantively linked to quantitative market-risk tables even though no internal edges are present here.

289.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure for banks using the Internal Models Approach (Table MRB), obligating description of IMA model scope, validation, and supervisory approval status.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Table MRB applies only to banks permitted to use IMA, making it a scope-limited disclosure obligation.
Logically subordinate to SAMA IMA model-approval requirements; complements the broader MRA market-risk narrative.

290.theme: Pillar 3 operational-risk qualitative disclosure (Table ORA), requiring banks to describe their operational-risk framework, policies, and measurement approach.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Table ORA sets a discrete qualitative disclosure requirement for the operational-risk regime.
Feeds from the bank's overall risk governance (see OVA) and pairs with quantitative operational-risk capital disclosures.

291.theme: Pillar 3 overarching risk-management disclosure (Table OVA), requiring banks to disclose their firm-wide risk management approach, appetite, and governance structure.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: Table OVA is the umbrella qualitative disclosure feeding the risk-specific tables (market, operational, credit).
Functions as the parent narrative from which regime-specific tables (MRA, MRB, ORA) draw governance context.

292.theme: Trading-book securitisation exposure disclosure under the capital/market-risk regime. Covers how banks must report securitisation positions held in the trading book for Pillar 3 transparency.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster (Template SEC2) with no internal edges; sits within the broader securitisation disclosure framework and is the quantitative counterpart to qualitative SECA (community 293).
Decision consequence: banks must populate this template to evidence trading-book securitisation capital treatment; it scopes reporting to trading-book (not banking-book) positions.

293.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure obligations for securitisation activity. Governs the narrative disclosures banks must make about their securitisation objectives, roles and risk management.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster (Table SECA) with no internal edges; complements the quantitative templates (e.g. SEC2, community 292) as the qualitative narrative layer.
Decision consequence: obliges banks to disclose their securitisation strategy and risk approach, giving supervisory and market readers context for the numeric exposures.

294.theme: Authenticity and verification of bank-issued documents. Addresses SAMA requirements for electronic issuance and independent verification of banking documents.
how_members_connect: Standalone provision with no mapped internal edges in the current graph.

Decision consequence: imposes an obligation on banks to enable electronic issuance/verification of documents, supporting anti-fraud and reliance by third parties; interacts with KYC/authentication expectations where documents evidence customer status.

295.theme: Personal data protection and data governance in the financial sector, anchoring the Kingdom's PDPL obligations onto SAMA-supervised entities.
how_members_connect: Standalone member with no internal edges; functions as the data-regime anchor that cross-cuts credit-information, consumer-protection and outsourcing obligations elsewhere in the graph.

Decision consequence: subordinates institutional data handling to the PDPL and associated governance duties (lawful processing, accountability), a cross-regime constraint on any customer-data use in AML, credit and payments contexts.

296.theme: Identification/KYC treatment of lawyers within customer due diligence, requiring capture of a National Unified Number when a lawyer acts as or on behalf of a customer. Relevant to onboarding and record-keeping under AML/CTF and consumer-facing identification rules.
how_members_connect: Single-member node imposing a specific identifier requirement (National Unified Number) for lawyers; functions as a defined-term/data-field obligation feeding broader CDD identification duties.
No internal edges provided — treat as a standalone identification control rather than part of an explicit obligation chain.

297.theme: Treatment of financing extended through National Development Fund banks, relevant to finance-company/lending scope, product classification, and any carve-outs or special conditions applying to state-development-fund credit.
how_members_connect: Single-member node identifying a specific loan category (National Development Fund bank loans); likely scopes or excepts these loans from ordinary finance/consumer-credit obligations.
No internal edges provided — standalone; its regulatory effect depends on cross-references to lending/consumer-protection regimes not shown here.

298.theme: Consumer protection disclosure requirement mandating standardised elements in customer notifications, ensuring uniform, minimum-content communications to customers.
how_members_connect: Single-member node imposing a content/format obligation on notifications sent to customers; a conduct/disclosure duty owed to the consumer.
No internal edges provided — operates as a discrete consumer-communication standard rather than part of a shown hierarchy.

299.theme: Consumer complaint-handling requirement prescribing a unified response template tied to the SAMA Cares framework, standardising how firms reply to customer complaints.
how_members_connect: Single-member node imposing a mandated response format for complaints, subordinate to SAMA's complaint-handling/consumer-protection regime (SAMA Cares).
No internal edges provided — standalone conduct obligation; complements standardised customer notifications (296/298 area) as part of consumer-facing communication duties.

300.theme: Interchange/scheme fee treatment for mada card claims within the national payments scheme, relevant to PSP and acquirer cost-allocation and consumer-charging rules.
how_members_connect: Single-member node addressing permissibility and allocation of fees arising on mada claims settlement.
No internal edges provided; treat as a standalone fee-rule reference under the payments regime rather than as part of an obligation chain.

301.theme: SMS notification service subscription rules, bearing on consumer-protection disclosure and customer-communication obligations for financial institutions.
how_members_connect: Single-member circular governing subscription/charging for SMS alert services.
No internal edges provided; use as a discrete consumer-protection/communications reference not yet linked to a parent regulation in this graph.

302.theme: Operational risk awareness relating to physical cash carrying/handling, touching security and consumer-safety guidance.
how_members_connect: Single awareness-oriented node with no cross-references in the provided context.
Treat as guidance-level material (awareness) rather than an enforceable standalone obligation absent a linked source regulation.

303.theme: Acceptance by financial institutions of electronically notarized LLC contracts, relevant to onboarding/KYB documentation standards and legal validity of e-notarized instruments.
how_members_connect: Single-member node establishing that e-notarized LLC contracts may be accepted, affecting corporate customer due-diligence document acceptance.
No internal edges provided; read alongside KYB/CDD requirements for legal-entity customers where those links exist elsewhere in the graph.

304.theme: Standing/authority of legal-department personnel to act as statutory representatives of a supervised entity in dealings with SAMA and other authorities.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: identifies who is legally empowered to represent the institution, bearing on validity of filings, notices, and undertakings.
Relevant to governance/accountability regimes where representation authority determines whether an act binds the entity.

305.theme: An image-based (scanned/non-machine-readable) SAMA circular; the format affects how the instrument is cited and relied upon as authority.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster representing a circular whose content is captured as an image, limiting extractable defined terms and article-level cross-references.
For legal decisions, treat as a subordinate SAMA instrument whose precise text must be verified against the original before reliance.

306.theme: SAMA circular addressing deeds issued by licensed notaries — relevant to documentary validity and evidentiary standing in financing/collateral contexts.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: governs recognition of notary-issued deeds, which underpins enforceability of secured transactions and title evidence.
Cross-relevant to real estate financing and CDD/documentation regimes where notarized instruments serve as proof.

307.theme: SAMA circular defining 'commercial real estate financing' — a scoping definition that determines which lending falls under the associated finance-company/real-estate financing regime.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster whose function is definitional: the defined term sets the perimeter of applicable prudential and consumer/finance rules.
Decision impact: classification as commercial vs. other real estate financing governs which obligations and limits apply.

308.theme: Standardization of the SME classification used across SAMA-supervised sectors. The circular fixes what counts as a micro/small/medium enterprise, which drives thresholds, reporting, and prudential/consumer treatments that turn on firm size.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: the circular is the authoritative source of the SME definition itself.
Functions as a definitional anchor other rules rely on when they scope obligations by enterprise size; no internal edges, so treat linkages to size-based provisions as external cross-references.

309.theme: Administrative modernization of documentary formalities. This circular removes the official-stamp requirement, affecting the validity/formality standard for accepted documents and correspondence.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: an amending/relaxing instrument that supersedes any prior requirement mandating an official stamp.
Legal consequence is that absence of a stamp can no longer be a basis to reject an otherwise valid document; check for other provisions that previously imposed the stamp.

310.theme: Transparency obligations around licensing status. Governs how supervised entities must disclose their SAMA license (e.g., in dealings, advertising, or public-facing statements).
how_members_connect: Single-member community: sets an affirmative disclosure duty on licensees regarding their authorization.
Interacts with consumer-protection and market-conduct regimes; the instruction constrains how firms may represent their regulated status.

311.theme: A scanned forms document (SAMA Doc 5783) — a template/forms artifact rather than a substantive rule-making instrument.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: supplies the operative forms referenced by an underlying obligation, not an independent obligation source.
Decision value depends on the parent instruction that mandates use of these forms; treat as an annex/attachment absent linked context.

312.theme: Governance/fit-and-proper regime covering approval of senior leadership appointments in SAMA-supervised institutions.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: an update to SAMA requirements governing appointment to leadership positions.
Legal effect is a prior-approval/notification obligation on the institution before senior appointments take effect; no internal cross-links are present in the provided context.

313.theme: Corporate social responsibility directive encouraging sector participation in a designated Social Responsibility Day.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster with no internal edges; stands alone as a discrete SAMA communication rather than an enforceable prudential rule.
Treat as a participation/contribution expectation, not a core compliance obligation, absent further linking context.

314.theme: Cyber/IT security control area (Security Information and Event Management) within SAMA's technology-risk governance framework.
how_members_connect: Single-member node referencing a security monitoring capability expected under SAMA cyber-security requirements.
No internal edges provided; on its own it indicates a control expectation rather than a standalone legal mandate.

315.theme: Unresolved SAMA source document (image-only) with no extracted regulatory text.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster; content is images only, so no defined terms, obligations, or cross-references can be established.
Not decision-useful until the document text is available; flag as incomplete rather than inferring scope or content.

316.theme: National Drug Prevention Project (Nebras) — a national initiative context that may prompt financial institutions to support prevention/awareness efforts, distinct from binding prudential or AML obligations.
how_members_connect: Single isolated node with no internal edges; stands alone as a named national program reference.
Decision impact: treat as awareness/participation context rather than an enforceable compliance obligation unless a specific SAMA circular ties banking conduct to it.

317.theme: Commitment to speedy enforcement of court judgments — governance/operational conduct expectation that supervised entities act promptly on judicial rulings.
how_members_connect: Isolated node; no cross-references in the graph to other regimes.
Decision impact: read as an enforceable expectation on institutions to execute court judgments without undue delay; verify the originating SAMA instruction before relying on scope.

318.theme: Controls for dealing with old or damaged bank equipment — operational/asset-disposal controls addressing secure handling and retirement of physical banking equipment.
how_members_connect: Standalone node with no internal linkages to AML, payments, or consumer regimes.
Decision impact: apply as operational governance controls; confirm data-security implications only if the underlying document extends to media/data-bearing equipment.

319.theme: SAMA Document 8359 (Scanned) — an unclassified source document whose regime and obligations cannot be determined from the graph alone.
how_members_connect: Isolated scanned-document node with no edges or defined-term linkage.
Decision impact: do not rely on for compliance conclusions until the document's subject matter, hierarchy (law/regulation/circular/guide), and obligations are identified from its actual text.

320.theme: Governs the circumstances under which a financial institution may or must disclose customer account data and block/freeze account balances — sitting at the intersection of bank-secrecy/data-protection duties and sanctions/TFS or law-enforcement freezing obligations.
how_members_connect: Single-member node: links disclosure permissions to balance-blocking as paired enforcement actions.
Compliance reading: disclosure and blocking are exceptions to ordinary confidentiality/customer-access rights, triggered by competent-authority order or TFS obligation.
No internal edges present; treat as a standalone provision pending cross-reference to AML/TFS and account-operation rules.

321.theme: Prudential governance/risk regime: the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP) reporting duty imposed on banks to demonstrate capital adequacy against their risk profile to SAMA.
how_members_connect: Single-member node capturing a recurring supervisory reporting obligation (who reports, to SAMA, on what cadence).
Subordinate to SAMA's capital-adequacy/risk-governance framework; ICAAP is the institution-side assessment feeding supervisory review.
No internal edges; standalone prudential obligation with no linked definitions in this cluster.

322.theme: Payments/technical-standards regime: a SAMA circular promulgating a guide on local technical products, i.e. the operational/technical rules for domestic payment products.
how_members_connect: Single-member node representing a circular-level instrument (below regulation, above pure guidance in the hierarchy).
Legal weight: circular issues binding technical requirements for in-scope payment/product participants.
No internal edges; standalone until cross-referenced to payment-scheme or PSP rules.

323.theme: Payments/consumer-protection regime: rules on fees for topping up e-wallets through the mada e-commerce channel — a pricing/fee-transparency matter affecting PSPs and wallet operators.
how_members_connect: Single-member node addressing permissible/charged fees on a specific mada wallet top-up flow.
Compliance reading: intersects fee-disclosure and consumer-protection obligations with payment-scheme (mada) participation rules.
No internal edges; standalone provision pending linkage to broader PSP fee and consumer-protection frameworks.

324.theme: AML/CTF designation of licensed real estate brokers as a Designated Non-Financial Business or Profession (DNFBP), subjecting them to customer due diligence and reporting duties despite being outside the core financial sector.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: real estate brokerage compliance treated as a distinct AML/CTF obligation set applicable to a licensed non-financial profession.

Legal consequence: obligations mirror CDD/KYC and suspicious-transaction reporting duties, but scoping is limited to brokerage activity thresholds — verify applicability before assuming full financial-institution obligations.

325.theme: Payments/PSP regime governing electronic payment services in the retail sector, defining licensing and operational conduct for payment activity at the merchant/consumer interface.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster covering retail electronic payment as a regulated payment activity under SAMA's payments framework.
Legal consequence: engagement in retail e-payment triggers PSP licensing/conduct obligations; note the merchant-as-customer (KYB) dimension where AML CDD duties may attach alongside payments rules.

326.theme: Data protection regime — compliance with the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) as it applies to financial-sector processing of personal data.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster anchoring PDPL obligations (lawful processing, consent, subject rights) for regulated entities.

Cross-regime note: PDPL obligations interact with AML record-keeping and credit-information sharing — where retention/disclosure is mandated by SAMA rules, that legal basis must be reconciled with PDPL limits.

327.theme: Governance/risk regime element — political risk as a category within enterprise and country-risk assessment for financial institutions.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster isolating political risk as a risk-management factor rather than a standalone obligation.

Legal consequence: relevant to risk-based approaches (e.g., country/geographic risk in AML/CTF and sanctions/TFS exposure) and to prudential governance expectations; not itself a prescriptive rule set.

328.theme: Corporate onboarding/formation documentation for entities being established as customers, bearing on KYB and legal-existence verification at account opening.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the circular addresses acceptance/handling of company establishment (incorporation) contracts as part of customer identification.
Relevant to CDD/KYB decisions where a legal person's constitutive documents evidence legal existence, ownership and authority to act.

329.theme: Wage Protection System obligations via the Mudad platform — an operational/regulatory expectation on employers and financial institutions to process salary payments through the designated channel.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the circular directs use of the Mudad platform for wage disbursement compliance.
Interacts with payments and account-servicing rules where institutions must support/route WPS salary transactions.

330.theme: Handling of entities whose commercial registers have been struck off — bearing on ongoing due diligence, account maintenance, and continued dealing with legal persons that have lost legal standing.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the circular transmits lists of struck-off commercial registers for institutions to act upon.
Feeds ongoing CDD/KYB and relationship-review obligations, since a struck-off registration undermines a customer's legal existence and authority.

331.theme: Scope/permissioning of payment services provided to entities operating within the Integrated Logistics Zone — a jurisdictional carve-out affecting which PSP rules apply to such entities.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the circular scopes payment services for a special-zone entity population.
Interacts with the general PSP/payments regime by defining or limiting how standard requirements apply to logistics-zone customers.

332.theme: Governs how financial institutions receive and act on judicial notifications delivered through an electronic mechanism, bridging court process and supervised entities' legal-obligation handling.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: a SAMA circular directing regulated entities on the electronic judicial notification channel.
Operates as a subordinate instrument implementing court/enforcement notification duties within the supervised sector; no internal cross-links present.

333.theme: Physical security and safety requirements for cash-in-transit operations, an operational-risk/security regime for supervised entities handling cash movement.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: a SAMA circular transmitting cash transport regulations plus a security/safety guide.
Circular functions as the binding cover; the accompanying guide sets the operational security standard—hierarchy of circular -> guide with no external edges provided.

334.theme: Identity-verification/CDD-adjacent guidance on treating expired national and resident (Iqama) IDs, relevant to KYC acceptance decisions and continued customer servicing.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: a SAMA circular on handling expired ID documents.
Bears on customer identification rules (potential AML/CDD and account-servicing interaction), though no linked AML instruments appear in this cluster.

335.theme: Labor/nationalization (Saudization) mandate applied to customer-service functions, a workforce-composition obligation on regulated entities issued outside SAMA's core prudential regime.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: a Ministerial Decision (No. 112203) mandating Saudization of customer-service roles.
External-authority instrument (Ministry, not SAMA) that supervised entities must observe alongside SAMA rules; standalone with no internal edges.
